The planning crew and greeting routines, minutes
It started on time, and the welfare lead led.

Andre Williams, Jonah Kim, and Teddy were present with the desk team.

The group checked in on the day-to-day flow at Aurelia Skyways and spoke about keeping the Companion Animal Travel Desk calm, clear, and welcoming for families and their animals. The senior coordinator reminded everyone that a kind first greeting helps settle travelers fast, especially when pets are uneasy after a long trip. The team agreed that plain language at the counter and in follow-up notes keeps handoffs smooth, and that small details such as labels, carrier checks, and quiet spacing can make the whole process easier.

The safety coordinator then walked through the main hazards seen in routine work, including crowded waiting areas, unsure carriers, and missed care instructions. The discussion stayed practical and focused on prevention, with the team agreeing to look twice at every pet tag, confirm feeding notes, and ask for clarification early when paperwork seems incomplete. There was also a reminder to keep water bowls, cleaning supplies, and spare forms in steady reach so no one has to rush while a pet is waiting nearby. Everyone liked the idea of keeping the desk tidy and calm as part of safety, not just appearance.

The department also shared a few simple service tips for crews. When a traveler arrives worried, a brief welcome, a steady voice, and a clear next step can lower stress right away. The team noted that when instructions are repeated in the same way each time, crews can help more easily and travelers feel less uncertain. It was agreed that helpful language should stay warm and direct, without extra jargon.

A few minor follow-ups were noted for the next round of desk work, mostly around keeping shared advice current and making sure everyone uses the same friendly tone. The group ended with a short reminder that consistency builds trust for animals and people alike, and that the desk does its best work when the whole team stays attentive and kind.

The meeting ended in good order.
